celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿أَلَمْ نَشْرَحْ﴾: an interrogative of affirmation (istifhām taqrīr), that is, We expanded ﴿لَكَ﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿صَدْرَكَ﴾ with prophethood and other things,

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿الَّذِي أَنْقَضَ﴾: weighed down ﴿ظَهْرَكَ﴾. This is like His words, Exalted is He, {لِيَغْفِرَ لَكَ اللَّهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِنْ ذَنْبِكَ}.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿وَرَفَعْنَا لَكَ ذِكْرَكَ﴾, in that you are mentioned along with My mention in the call to prayer, the iqāma, the tashahhud, the sermon and elsewhere.

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿إِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا﴾: the Prophet ﷺ suffered hardship from the disbelievers, then ease came to him through his victory over them.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿فَإِذَا فَرَغْتَ﴾ from the prayer ﴿فَانْصَبْ﴾: exert yourself in supplication,

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿أَلَمْ نَشْرَحْ﴾: the hamza is a particle of interrogation and affirmation (taqrīr), and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); ﴿لَكَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿صَدْرَكَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿وَوَضَعْنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿عَنْكَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿وِزْرَكَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿الَّذِي﴾: a relative noun, naʿt (adjective) of وزرك; ﴿أَنْقَضَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿ظَهْرَكَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿وَرَفَعْنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿لَكَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿ذِكْرَكَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿فَإِنَّ﴾: the fāʾ is a resumptive particle and ﴿إن﴾ is a particle resembling the verb (one of inna and its sisters); ﴿مَعَ﴾: an adverb of place, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of inna; ﴿الْعُسْرِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿يُسْراً﴾: the postponed noun of inna; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:6-6.t: A tawkīd (emphasis) of the preceding verse.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿فَإِذا﴾: the fāʾ is a resumptive particle; ﴿إذا﴾: a conditional adverb that does not put the verb in the jussive; ﴿فَرَغْتَ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); ﴿فَانْصَبْ﴾: the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ (rābiṭa), and an imperative verb whose agent is latent (mustatir); the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and has no grammatical position, and the clause إذا… is resumptive.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿وَإِلى رَبِّكَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what follows them; ﴿فَارْغَبْ﴾: the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

farraa:1-1.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَلَمْ نَشْرَحْ لَكَ صَدْرَكَ﴾.
[Did We not] soften your heart for you?

farraa:2-2.t: ﴿وَوَضَعْنَا عَنكَ وِزْرَكَ﴾: he says: the sin of the Jāhiliyya. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [Translator's note: Ibn Masʿūd] it is: "وحللنا عنك وِقْرك" (and We untied from you your load); he says: of sins.

farraa:3-3.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلَّذِيۤ أَنقَضَ ظَهْرَكَ﴾.
In the tafsīr of al-Kalbī: which weighed down your back, meaning the burden (الوِزر).

farraa:4-4.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَرَفَعْنَا لَكَ ذِكْرَكَ﴾.
I am not mentioned without your being mentioned with Me.

farraa:5-5.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِنَّ مَعَ ٱلْعُسْرِ يُسْراً﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [Translator's note: Ibn Masʿūd] [it occurs] once only, not repeated. He said: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us; he said: Ḥibbān narrated to me from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: One hardship will not overcome two eases.

farraa:7-7.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِذَا فَرَغْتَ فَٱنصَبْ﴾.
When you have finished your prayer, then exert yourself toward your Lord in supplication and be desirous. Al-Farrāʾ said: «فانصب» is from النَّصَب (toil).
Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us; he said: Muḥammad narrated to us; he said: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us; he said: Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ, from Abū Ḥaṣīn, who said: Shurayḥ passed by two men wrestling, and he said: It is not this that the one who is free (al-fārigh) was commanded to do; Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, only said: ﴿فَإِذَا فَرَغْتَ فَٱنصَبْ وَإِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ فَٱرْغَبْ﴾. So it is as if, in Shurayḥ's view, [it means]: when the one who has finished is done with prayer or with something else.

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: (فإن مع العسر يسرا) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive; «مع»: an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: (إن مع العسر يسرا) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: (فإذا فرغت فانصب) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The conditional clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: (وإلى ربك فارغب) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The fāʾ links the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: if you ask, then turn with longing to your Lord; and the conditional clause is conjoined to the preceding one.

mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, the Exalted: (ألم نشرح): the alif [i.e. the interrogative hamza] has transferred the speech from negation and turned it into an affirmation.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿ألم﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (taqrīrī), and «لم» is a particle of negation, jussive and conversion (to the past).
﴿نشرح﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لم﴾, and its agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "We" (نحن).
﴿لك﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نشرح﴾.
﴿صدرك﴾: «صدر» is mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the kāf is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the clause ﴿ألم نشرح﴾ is initial (ibtidāʾiyya).

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿ووضعنا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive and «وضعنا» is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, and the pronoun is in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿ووضعنا﴾ is conjoined to ﴿ألم نشرح﴾.
﴿عنك﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿وضعنا﴾.
﴿وزرك﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and the kāf is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿الذي﴾: a relative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿وزرك﴾.
﴿أنقض﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "it" (هو).
﴿ظهرك﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and the kāf is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the clause ﴿أنقض﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿الذي﴾.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿ورفعنا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and «رفعنا» is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, and the pronoun is in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent); «رفعنا» is conjoined to ﴿ألم نشرح﴾.
﴿لك﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿رفعنا﴾.
﴿ذكرك﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and the kāf is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿فإن﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive, with no grammatical position; «إن» is an abrogating particle.
﴿مع﴾: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate).
﴿العسر﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr).
﴿يسرا﴾: the postponed noun (ism) of «إن», accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the overt fatḥa.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿إن﴾: an abrogating particle.
﴿مع﴾: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate).
﴿العسر﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr).
﴿يسرا﴾: the postponed noun (ism) of «إن»; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿فإذا﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive, conjoining to something implied that the context calls for, or the wāw [Translator's note: so in the source; the word begins with a fāʾ] is resumptive and the clause after it is resumptive, with no grammatical position; «إذا» is an adverb of future time containing the sense of condition, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the answer.
﴿فرغت﴾: a past verb, and the tāʾ is the fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿فرغت﴾ is in the position of genitive by the adverb being annexed to it.
﴿فانصب﴾: the fāʾ is linking (rābiṭa), and «انصب» is an imperative verb, and the agent is latent (mustatir); the clause has no grammatical position, because it is the answer of a non-jussive condition.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿و﴾: conjunctive.
﴿إلى ربك﴾: «إلى» is a preposition and the word ﴿رب﴾ is a noun in the genitive (majrūr), and the kāf is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ارغب﴾.
﴿فارغب﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ of eloquence (al-faṣīḥa) and «ارغب» is an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
نَشْرَحْ is jussive (majzūm) by لم, and the mark of the jussive is the dropping of the ḍamma. Among the grammarians are those who say that «ألم» is one of the jussive particles, and that is a mistake, because the alif is for the interrogative. The meaning is affirmative, because the interrogative alif here conveys the sense of establishing (taqrīr) and making (the addressee) acknowledge, so the negative becomes affirmative and the affirmative negative.
Al-Farrāʾ said: i.e., "Did We not soften your heart for you?" And al-Ḥusayn ibn Wāqid said: "Did We not widen your breast for you?" Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a clear view; from it one says: "so-and-so is narrow of breast" and "his breast is wide". Allah has expanded the breasts of the prophets, Allah's blessings be upon them, and of the believers, as a reward for their good deeds, so they came to accept the truth and their breasts did not become constricted by it. From this is the ḥadīth with a sound chain, which Yūnus narrated from al-Zuhrī, from Anas, from Abū Dharr, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: «The roof of my house was opened while I was in Mecca, and Jibrīl ﷺ descended and opened my breast, then washed it with Zamzam water, then brought a basin filled with wisdom and faith and placed it in my breast, then ascended with me to the heaven».
لَكَ: the kāf is in the position of the genitive by the lām, and the lām took fatḥa according to its origin. Among the grammarians are those who say: its origin is kasra, but it took fatḥa in their saying له so as not to combine a kasra and a ḍamma, and then «لك» was made to follow له, even though that reason does not exist in it. صَدْرَكَ is accusative by نشرح. The scholars said: the breast is the seat of the Qur'an and of knowledge, and they took as evidence for that the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: بَلْ هُوَ آياتٌ بَيِّناتٌ فِي صُدُورِ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ [al-ʿAnkabūt: 49].

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: Al-Ḥasan said: his burden (wizr) is his sin in the Jāhiliyya. One says: wazara yaziru wizran, and the passive participle is mawzūr; and in the ḥadīth: «Return burdened (mawzūrāt), not rewarded (maʾjūrāt)». Some of the ḥadīth scholars say «maʾzūrāt»; if its transmission is sound, it is for harmony (itbāʿ, with maʾjūrāt).

nahhas-irab:3-3.t:
The exegetes say: (أنقض means) weighed it down. If someone says: how was this burden described as heavy when it is forgiven and not demanded of him? The answer is that the way of the prophets, Allah's blessings be upon them, and of the righteous is that when they remember their sins their grief and weeping intensify; for this reason their sins were described as heavy. Abū Jaʿfar said:
And this is the answer to the question of the one who asks: why do the righteous grieve when they remember their sins from which they have repented, when they know that forgiveness after repentance is certain? There is another answer to this, namely that they fear that something may remain upon them that is required of them to complete the repentance.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: The explanation of this is in the ḥadīth with a connected chain (musnad) from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: Jibrīl ﷺ said to me: «Your Lord and my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, says to you: How have I raised your mention? He said: I said: Allah knows best. He said: When I am mentioned, you are mentioned with Me».

nahhas-irab:5-6.t: ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read with ḍamma on the sīn in both (al-ʿusur, yusuran). It has been said: the meaning is that the favours of Allah the Exalted, which are the ease, are more than the hardships, which are the difficulty. And it has been said: the Prophet ﷺ was addressed with (the news) that he would be victorious, and that victory — which is the ease — would be over the idolaters from whom hardship had befallen (him).

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: Abū Jaʿfar said: We have mentioned what has been said about the repetition, and what has been said about the meaning of فَإِذا فَرَغْتَ فَانْصَبْ (7). Among the best things said about it, and it comprehends all the views, is that when a person finishes his occupation he should stand up (yantaṣib) for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and turn to Him in longing, and not busy himself with what distracts him from the remembrance of Allah, Glorified. This is the discipline (adab) of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said: I am not pleased by a person whom I see idle, busying himself neither with the affair of this world nor with the affair of the Hereafter.

semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {أَلَمْ نَشْرَحْ}: When the interrogative enters upon a negation it affirms it, so the meaning becomes: "We have indeed expanded"; that is why a past verb is conjoined to it. Similar to it is {أَلَمْ نُرَبِّكَ فِينَا وَلِيداً وَلَبِثْتَ} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 18]. The majority read the ḥāʾ with the jussive (jazm) by «لم», and Abū Jaʿfar read it with fatḥa. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «They said: perhaps he articulated the ḥāʾ distinctly and gave it its full value at its point of articulation, so the listener thought he gave it fatḥa.» Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: «The original is "ألم نَشْرَحَنْ" with the light nūn [of emphasis]; then he replaced it with an alif, then omitted it for lightness», as Abū Zayd quoted:
4597 - مِنْ أيِّ يَوْمَيَّ من الموتِ أفِرّْ ... أيومَ لم يُقْدَرَ أم يومَ قُدِرْ
(From which of my two days shall I flee death: the day it is not decreed, or the day it is decreed?)
with fatḥa on the rāʾ of «لم يُقْدَرَ»; and like his saying:
4598 - اضْرِبَ عنكَ الهمومَ طارِقَها ... ضَرْبَكَ بالسيفِ قَوْنَسَ الفَرَسِ
(Strike away from you the cares that come by night, as you strike with the sword the crest of the horse.)
with fatḥa on the bāʾ of «اضربَ». End of quotation. This is built on the permissibility of emphasising [with the nūn] a verb made jussive by «لم», which is very rare, as in his saying:
4599 - يَحْسَبُه الجاهلُ ما لم يَعْلما ... شيخاً على كُرْسِيِّه مُعَمَّما
(The ignorant one, as long as he does not know, takes him for a turbaned elder on his chair.)
So this reading is composed of three bases, all of them weak: because emphasising a verb made jussive by «لم» is weak; replacing it [the nūn] with an alif belongs only to the pause, and treating continuous speech like the pause is contrary to the basic rule; and omitting the alif is weak, because it is contrary to the basic rule. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] explained it according to a dialect that al-Liḥyānī related in his «Nawādir» from some Arabs, namely the jussive by «لن» and the subjunctive by «لم», the reverse of what is known among people, and he considered this better than the preceding. He quoted the saying of ʿĀʾisha bint al-Aʿjam praising al-Mukhtār, who rose to seek vengeance for al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with them both:
4600 - قد كادَ سَمْكُ الهدى يُنْهَدُّ قائمُهُ ... حتى أتيحَ له المختارُ فانْعَمدا
في كلِّ ما هَمَّ أمضى رأيَه قُدُماً ... ولم يُشاوِرَ في إقدامِه أحدا
(The roof of guidance had nearly had its pillar collapse, until al-Mukhtār was granted to it and it was propped up. In everything he resolved upon he carried out his judgement boldly, and consulted no one in his advance.)
with fatḥa on the rāʾ of «يُشاور», and he considered it open to both explanations.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {أَنقَضَ ظَهْرَكَ}, i.e. it made it produce النقيض, which is the sound of cracking and coming apart because of its heaviness — a parable for what used to weigh upon him ﷺ. The lexicographers said: أَنْقَضَ الحِمْلُ ظَهْرَ الناقةِ (the load made the she-camel's back creak) when you hear a creaking from it because of the severity of the load; and سمِعْتُ نقيضَ الرَّحْلِ, i.e. its creaking. Al-ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās said:
4601 - وأَنْقَضَ ظهري ما تَطَوَّيْتَ منهمُ ... وكنتُ عليهم مُشْفِقاً مُتَحَنِّناً
(What you concealed against them made my back creak, while I was compassionate and tender toward them.)
And Jamīl said:
4602 - وحتى تداعَتْ بالنَّقيضِ حِبالُه ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(…until its ropes called out to one another with creaking…)

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {فَإِنَّ مَعَ العسر يُسْراً}: The majority read with sukūn on the sīn in the four words, and Ibn Waththāb, Abū Jaʿfar and ʿĪsā with ḍamma on it. There is disagreement about it: is it [the ḍamma form] original, or made heavy from the quiescent form? The alif and lām in the first «العُسر» are for the definiteness of the genus, and in the second for prior reference (ʿahd); that is why it is related from Ibn ʿAbbās: «One hardship will never overcome two eases»; and it is also related as a saying of the Prophet (marfūʿ) that he, peace be upon him, came out laughing, saying: «One hardship will never overcome two eases.» The reason for it is that when the Arabs bring a noun and then repeat it with the alif and lām, it is the same as the first, e.g. «جاء رجلٌ فأكرمْتُ الرجلَ» (a man came and I honoured the man), and as in His saying, the Exalted: {كَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَآ إلى فِرْعَوْنَ رَسُولاً فعصى فِرْعَوْنُ الرسول} [al-Muzzammil: 15–16]; and if they repeat it without alif and lām, it is other than the first. So in His saying: {إِنَّ مَعَ العسر يُسْراً}, when He repeated the second hardship He repeated it with «أل», and since the second ease is other than the first, He did not repeat it with «أل».
Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you say: what is the meaning of the saying of Ibn ʿAbbās? — and he mentioned what has preceded — I say: this is acting on the apparent sense and building on the strength of hope, and [on the principle] that Allah's promise is to be taken only in the fullest and most far-reaching sense the wording admits. What is to be said about it is that it is possible that the second clause is a repetition of the first, just as He repeated His saying: {وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِّلْمُكَذِّبِينَ} [al-Mursalāt: 15] to establish its meaning in the souls and fix it in the hearts, and just as the single word is repeated in your saying: "جاء زيدٌ زيدٌ" (Zayd came, Zayd); and it is possible that the first is a promise that hardship is inevitably followed by ease, and the second a new promise that hardship is followed by ease, so they are two eases on the supposition of a new statement. The hardship is one only because it must be either that its definiteness is for prior reference, namely the hardship they were in, so it is the same; because its rule is the rule of "زيد" in your saying: "إنَّ مع زيد مالاً، إنَّ مع زيد مالاً" (Zayd has wealth, Zayd has wealth); or that it is for the genus that everyone knows, so it is also the same. As for ease, it is indefinite, covering part of the genus; and if the second statement is a new one, not a repetition, it covers a part other than the first part, without any difficulty.»
Abū al-Baqāʾ said: «The hardship in the two places is one, because the alif and the lām require the repetition of the first. As for "يُسْراً" in the two places, they are two, because when an indefinite noun is meant to be repeated, its pronoun or the alif and lām is brought; and from here it was said: "One hardship will never overcome two eases".» Al-Zamakhsharī also said: «If you say: "مع" is for accompaniment, so what is the meaning of the accompaniment of ease and hardship? I say: He meant that Allah the Exalted would bring them ease after the hardship they were in, within a short time; so He brought the awaited ease near, until He made it as though it were joined to the hardship, as an increase in consolation and a strengthening of hearts.» He also said: «If you say: what is the meaning of this indefiniteness? I say: magnification, as though it were said: with hardship is a mighty ease, and what an ease! In the codex of Ibn Masʿūd it is [written] only once. If you say: if it is established in his reading unrepeated, why did he [the Prophet] say: "By Him in Whose hand is my soul, if hardship were in a hole, ease would seek it until it entered upon it; one hardship will never overcome two eases"? I say: it is as though by the two eases he intended the sense of magnification in His saying "يُسْراً", so he interpreted it as "the ease of the two abodes", and that is in reality two eases.»

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {فَإِذَا فَرَغْتَ}: The majority read «فَرَغْتَ» with fatḥa on the rāʾ, and it is the well-known [form]; Abū al-Sammāl read it with kasra, and it is a minor dialectal form; al-Zamakhsharī said: «It is not the eloquent one.» Al-Zamakhsharī [also] said: «If you say: how is His saying "فإذا فَرَغْتَ فانصَبْ" connected with what precedes it? I say: when He enumerated His past favours and His forthcoming promise, He urged him to gratitude and to striving in worship. From Ibn ʿAbbās: when you have finished your prayer, then exert yourself in supplication.»
The majority read with fatḥa on the ṣād and sukūn on the bāʾ, as an imperative from النَّصَب (toil). It was also read with doubling of the bāʾ, with fatḥa, as an imperative from الانْصباب (pouring forth). [Translator's note: the source has «متفوحة», evidently for «مفتوحة» (with fatḥa).] Likewise it was read with kasra on the ṣād and sukūn on the bāʾ, as an imperative from النَّصْب (setting up) with sukūn on the ṣād. I do not consider the first anything but a misreading of the dots (taṣḥīf), nor the second anything but a distortion (taḥrīf), for it is related from the Imāmiyya, and their interpretation of it is: when you have finished with prophethood, then appoint the caliph. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: «It is a weak, irregular (shādhdh) reading not established from any scholar.» Al-Zamakhsharī said: «Among the innovations is what is related from some of the Rāfiḍa, that he read "فانصِبْ", i.e. appoint ʿAlī to the imamate; and if this were valid for the Rāfiḍī, it would be valid for the Nāṣibī to read it thus and make it a command to النَّصْب, which is hatred of ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, and enmity toward him.»

semin-durr:8-8.t: His saying: {فارغب}: from الرَّغْبة (desire). Zayd ibn ʿAlī and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «فَرَغِّب» with doubling of the middle radical, as an imperative from رَغَّبَه with doubling, i.e. make people desire to seek what is with Him. [Translator's note: the source writes the reading as «فَرَغَّب», but its own gloss «فَرَغِّب» shows the imperative form.]

ukberi-tibyan:5-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَإِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا (٥) إِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا (٦)).
(الْعُسْرِ) in both places is one and the same, because the alif and lām (the definite article) require the repetition of the first. As for «يُسْرًا» in both places, they are two, because when an indefinite noun is meant to be repeated, its pronoun or the alif and lām is brought; from this it was said: «لَنْ يَغْلِبَ عُسْرٌ يُسْرَيْنِ» (one hardship will never overcome two eases). And Allah knows best.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Sharḥ
Meccan
﷽
His saying: ﴿ألَمْ نَشْرَحْ لَكَ صَدْرَكَ﴾ ("did We not expand for you your breast?"): that is, We expanded it for Islam.

zajjaj:2-2.t: ﴿وَوَضَعْنا عَنْكَ وِزْرَكَ﴾ ("and We removed from you your burden"): that is, We removed from you your sin, in that Allah forgave you your former and later sins.

zajjaj:3-4.t: ﴿الَّذِي أنْقَضَ ظَهْرَكَ﴾ ﴿وَرَفَعْنا لَكَ ذِكْرَكَ﴾ ("which weighed down your back, and We raised high your mention"): He made the mention of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ joined with the mention of Allah's oneness in the call to prayer, and in much of that in which Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, is mentioned, where one says: ”أشْهَدُ أنْ لا إلَهَ إلّا اللَّهُ، أشْهَدَ أنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ“ ("I bear witness that there is no god but Allah; I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah").

zajjaj:5-5.t: And His saying: ﴿فَإنَّ مَعَ العُسْرِ يُسْرًا﴾ ("for with hardship comes ease"): He mentioned "the hardship" with the alif and lām, then repeated its mention, so the meaning became: "with the hardship are two eases". And the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: «”لا يَغْلِبُ عُسْرٌ يُسْرَيْنِ“» ("one hardship will not overcome two eases"); and it was said: «”لَوْ دَخَلَ العُسْرُ جُحْرًا لَدَخَلَ اليُسْرُ عَلَيْهِ“» ("if hardship entered a burrow, ease would enter in upon it"). That is because the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ were in severe straits, so Allah let them know that they would become well off and that [victories] would be opened to them, and He exchanged for them hardship with ease.

zajjaj:8-8.t: And His saying: ﴿وَإلى رَبِّكَ فارْغَبْ﴾ ("and to your Lord direct your longing"): that is, make your longing toward Allah alone.
